title: Design Linked List
prompt:
Design your own singly linked list implementation supporting: `get(index)` (the value at `index`, or `-1` if out of range), `addAtHead(val)`, `addAtTail(val)`, `addAtIndex(index, val)` (inserts before the node currently at `index`; inserting at `index` equal to the list's length appends at the tail; an index greater than the length is a no-op; a negative index is treated as inserting at the head), and `deleteAtIndex(index)` (removes the node at `index` if it's valid, otherwise does nothing). The list is 0-indexed.

You'll implement this as a single function `runLinkedListOps(ops)`, where `ops` is an array of `[operationName, args...]` entries applied in order to one list instance: `addAtHead`, `addAtTail`, `addAtIndex`, and `deleteAtIndex` never produce output, while `get` pushes its return value onto the output array. Return the output array.

examples.explanation: addAtHead(1) -> [1]. addAtTail(3) -> [1,3]. addAtIndex(1,2) -> [1,2,3]. get(0)=1, get(1)=2, get(2)=3. deleteAtIndex(0) -> [2,3]. get(0)=2.

addAtHead(7) -> [7]. addAtHead(2) -> [2,7]. addAtHead(1) -> [1,2,7]. addAtIndex(3,0) appends since index equals the length -> [1,2,7,0]. deleteAtIndex(2) removes the node at index 2 (value 7) -> [1,2,0]. get(0)=1, get(1)=2, get(2)=0.
On an empty list, get(0) is out of range and returns -1. deleteAtIndex(0) and addAtIndex(5,10) both target indices beyond the (empty) list's bounds, so they're no-ops and produce no output.

constraints: At most 2000 total calls across all operations
hints: A dummy head node before the real first node removes the need to special-case insertions or deletions at position 0.
For get/addAtIndex/deleteAtIndex, you need to walk from the dummy head the right number of steps to reach the node just before the target position.
Keep a running size count so you can quickly reject out-of-range indices without an extra traversal, and so addAtIndex(length, val) — appending — is handled the same way as any other valid index.

solution.approach: Maintain a dummy head node and a size counter. Every operation reduces to walking from the dummy the correct number of steps to reach the node just before the target position, then reading or rewiring `next` pointers there. get(index) and deleteAtIndex(index) are no-ops/return -1 when index is out of [0, size), addAtIndex clamps negative indices to 0 and rejects index > size, and addAtHead/addAtTail are just addAtIndex(0, val) and addAtIndex(size, val) respectively. Keeping size updated on every insert/delete makes every operation O(index) instead of needing a separate length-counting pass.
